claims.statement: For D_m^perp(S)=sum_{|R|=|C|=m,RcapC=empty} det(S[R,C])^2 there is an original-coordinate cut L|Rside with e_m(S[L,Rside]^T S[L,Rside]) >= 4^{-m} D_m^perp(S); a theta-random cut has exact expectation theta^m(1-theta)^m D_m^perp(S).
For original scalar pivot a=A_kk !=0 and residual Schur complement S, B_{m+1,k}^perp(A)=a^2 D_m^perp(S).

If A_kk !=0 and B_{4,k}^perp(A)>0, then arbitrary cap-one product inputs satisfy ||p_Q||_infinity < 16.018 (|A_kk|^4 B_{4,k}^perp(A))^{-1/12}. Essential boundedness is proved; continuity is not claimed.

If A_kk !=0 and B_{3,k}^perp(A)>0, either ||p_Q||_infinity <17.576 (|A_kk|^2 B_{3,k}^perp(A))^{-1/8}, or there are physical i,j !=k with complete disjoint trihub energy J_{k;i,j}^perp(A)>B_{3,k}^perp(A)/288.

The unfinished 20260923T043329Z B13 checkpoint's 22.653 cross-three cut-free constant double-counted the random-cut factor sqrt(2). The corrected safe constant is 16.018, from 11.3261681574*64^{1/12}=16.017620618.

designated_partner_application.application: Corollary 2.2 transfers the new paid geometric slab inequalities from bounded finite-union unit product indicators to all cap-one product laws with zero constant loss, and extracts extreme-product witnesses for strict violations.
